speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; may I ask how long it has been present and what, if anything, triggered it? Also, have you noticed any fever, chills, or swollen lymph nodes near the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis. The combination of a leg ulcer with a specific "ant bite" history, plus your immunocompromised state due to Crohn's disease, diabetes, and steroid use for uveitis, strongly points to Leishmania infection. I recommend a skin biopsy and Giemsa stain to confirm the presence of amastigotes before starting treatment.
